families.scaffolding_and_connected_parts: Conversion and evaluation are distinct outputs when both asked;do not omit the former.
families.alternative_methods: Definition a^x=b⇔log_a b=x,exact power/root recognition and the permitted calculator for approximate evaluations.
families.units_and_precision: Preserve original positive-argument/base restrictions and exact logarithmic boundaries. Source decimal cutoffs are displays,not replacement inequality endpoints. insights.title: Index/log definitions,laws and original-domain equivalence
insights.teaching_comparison: YM explicitly converts notation in both directions before exact evaluation,expansion/compression and solving. Goldie begins from exponential graphs/common-base reasoning and physical logarithmic-scale contexts. Both expand and compress within a base;neither route authorises requiring the excluded change-of-base theorem. YM6’sprinted positive-factor expansions can be narrower than the original squared-product domain;the inventory records both the source convention and absolute-log extension.
insights.examination_comparison: NSSCAS2024P2Q3uses log laws and original arguments in a solve. Standalone conversion/no-calculator definitions and subject-change tasks are lower scaffolds,not whole-exam coverage. The official source-specific log-domain rule remains separate from generic algebraic simplification. A negative variable is valid when each actual log argument is positive.
insights.difficulty_and_grade_bounds: E11/C11/A12include logarithm-index relation and laws. Difficulty changes through original domain,variable base,correlated simultaneous pairs and target form;it is not determined by whether thebaseis10ore.
